audience.rationale: Required by the objective, not inferred from an artifact: the objective's correction ('not the first sentence') only operates addressed to someone who holds the first-sentence picture, and the steering examples the concept is performed with (re-steering for a family member, against an engineer's register) are the general viewer's own acts, not a specialist's. The lane confirms the address: Word Definitions writes for a first-time viewer of the term (canon audience: general public, plain words; GOAL.md series rules).
audience.record: GOAL.md (audience: general public) + the phase-1 objective (this file)
audience.source: archer reasoning (this branch, phase 1, 2026-10-26) — required by the phase-1 objective; the lane's audience pattern as corroboration
audience.value: The general-public viewer who uses a chat AI and believes their prompt was the first message they typed — which is nearly every user. Secondarily, the would-be builder who already steers mid-job ('warmer, shorter, for my mother') but has no name for what the steering adds up to. The misconception the piece corrects: 'My prompt is the sentence I started with; everything after that is just chatting.'

delivery_structure.rationale: Iteration 1's pattern stands for M1–M5 (identical lines, identical joints). Inside M6 the joints are sized by the mechanism's own rhythm: the chain must be seen forming more than once, so L7's internal beats carry the repetition and the L7→L8 joint stays at working pace (0.55 s — the instrument is picked up, not contemplated); the extraction→naming joint widens (0.70 s) so the aspects land before the name is given; naming→practice is statement pace (0.50 s); and the piece's most expensive second — the designed silence — migrates from iteration 1's L7→L8 joint to L10→L11, because the payoff's position moved: the silence must hold whatever now stands immediately before the verdict.
delivery_structure.source: archer reasoning (this branch, phase 8, 2026-10-26), derived from the phase-2 delivery pattern + the iteration-2 story structure
delivery_structure.value: Definition cadence over the six moves: statement (M1) → SUSPENSION → turn (M2) → performed example with tight joints (M3) → mechanism widen (M4) → accumulation claim (M5) → the gathering taught at working pace (M6 i–iv: chain → extraction → naming → practice, joints 0.50–0.70 s by joint function) → DESIGNED SILENCE → payoff (M6 verdict) → bridge under bed only. Inter-line gaps are sized in transcript/delivery.md (iteration 2): the misconception→correction suspension 0.90 s; the pre-payoff designed silence 1.00 s (migrated to the new last joint, L10→L11); lead-in 0.40 s; tail 2.00 s. The music bed is continuous throughout — pauses are narration events, never bed cuts (the owner's standing rule).

end_referral.rationale: Owner direction (2026-10-26, ~14:22 ET): 'relay back to our direction video — if you want to understand how a prompt can be a direction, watch this other video — you can even plug that at the end.' The card carries his sentence as its question, per the established end-referral practice (silent card, bed only, the payoff never talked over). This SUPERSEDES the phase-2 derivation (a WD-04 'What Is Context?' card, derived by Archer from M4's mechanism): the owner's relay names the concept this piece's first half teaches — a prompt IS a direction — and the direction piece is where that claim is grounded; the revision and its reason are recorded here and in the register (progressive consolidation: a downstream owner direction revises an upstream Archer derivation, in the open). The ambiguity in his wording (spoken plug vs card) is NOT silently resolved: the established practice is the card, the transcript is unchanged by the referral either way, and the spoken alternative is flagged for him in the iteration-2 report — if he wants it spoken, it is one added line next iteration.
end_referral.record: phase-8 story_structure + end_referral (this file); scene/scene.json compartment C7 (phase 9); register R-9
end_referral.source: the owner's direction (2026-10-26, ~14:22 ET), via transcript/consolidation.md (iteration 2) — supersedes archer reasoning (phase 2)
end_referral.value: Silent bridge card in the final seconds, over the held payoff: 'NEXT — how a prompt can be a direction / A WORD IS A DIRECTION →'. Target: ws01-v2 'A Word Is a Direction' (the lane's direction piece — the piece the DIR trio's closers relay to). Bed only, no narration; navigation load = the card's ~2 s tail, 0% of the narration.

hook_form.rationale: The lane's definition contract: name the belief, break it, define. The hook's job for this objective is to put the viewer's own picture on the table in their own terms, because the piece's whole work is replacing that picture; a performed cold-open (the rejected build's form: two answers, cause withheld) spends the hook on an effect and then has to spend more lines explaining it — seconds this objective needs for the mechanism. The correction arriving inside the second line is the retention beat: the viewer who almost scrolled on a familiar claim stays for the break in it.
hook_form.record: phase-1 objective (this file); scene/scene.json compartment C1 (phase 4)
hook_form.source: archer reasoning (this branch, phase 2, 2026-10-26), from the phase-1 objective + the lane's misconception-correction pattern
hook_form.value: The misconception itself, stated plainly in the first line and corrected by the second (inside ~5 s): 'Most people think a prompt is the first sentence you type into the chat.' → 'It is not. A prompt is a direction…' No tease debt, no performed cold-open. The familiar anchor: every viewer typed a first sentence into a chat today. On screen the flat picture is DRAWN — a lone prompt card tagged THE PROMPT — so the hook is seen as well as heard.

message.rationale: The message is the definition compressed to its repeatable form: direction (the concept) + accumulated (its scope). Five words, each load-bearing — drop 'accumulated' and the message collapses back into the rejected single-moment definition; drop 'direction' and it loses the owner's concept for a synonym. The essence form was proposed in this morning's redevelopment draft (Candidate B's record); it is adopted here because the derivation re-checks out from the owner's definition directly, not because the draft carried it. The viewer restatement is the same sentence in the viewer's own likely words — the lane's restatement test.
message.record: hidden_files/wd02-redevelop/staging/transcript/redevelopment-draft-2026-10-26.md §2 (proposed essence) — cited as the proposal this decision adopts, with the derivation above as its ground
message.source: archer reasoning (this branch, phase 1, 2026-10-26), from the owner's definition (2026-10-26)
message.value: A prompt is accumulated direction. (Viewer restatement: 'The prompt is all the steering, not the first line.')

objective.rationale: Derived from the piece's purpose, not from any earlier artifact: wd-02 is the Word Definitions lane's definition of 'prompt', the term the whole Academy doctrine runs on (the user directs; the agent's context is what gets directed). The objective is stated as the viewer change the definition must produce: the viewer arrives holding the flat picture (the prompt = the first sentence typed) and must leave able to say the prompt is the accumulated directions. 16 words. The definition's content is the owner's own ruling of 2026-10-26 — the piece teaches HIS concept, so the objective names exactly his two moves: not-the-first-sentence (the correction) and every-direction-accumulated (the concept).
objective.record: MEMORY.md (the owner's prompt definition, 2026-10-26) + hidden_files/wd02-redevelop/staging/transcript/redevelopment-draft-2026-10-26.md §1 (his framing, quoted)
objective.source: archer reasoning (this branch, phase 1, 2026-10-26) — from the lane's purpose (Word Definitions: define the term for a first-time viewer) + the owner's definition of 'prompt' (2026-10-26, ~11:50 ET)
objective.value: Teach that a prompt is not the first sentence but every direction the user gives, accumulated.

role.rationale: The lane's division of labour: a Word Definitions piece introduces its term completely inside its own minute, because the funnel cannot presume viewing order. The objective is a definition-transfer (the viewer leaves able to say what a prompt is), which is INTRODUCE work, not APPLY work — no doctrine is applied here; the concept itself is the payload.
role.record: phase-1 objective (this file); the catalogue 'direction' thread noted as resonance, not dependency
role.source: archer reasoning (this branch, phase 2, 2026-10-26), from the phase-1 objective + the lane's role pattern
role.value: INTRODUCE — define the word 'prompt' for a first-time viewer. The piece presumes nothing from any other video: WD-01's 'direction' thread (a token is 'the smallest piece of text that gets one [a direction]') is a resonance a returning viewer may feel, never a dependency the arc leans on.

scene_decomposition.rationale: Prescribed from the iteration-2 story structure: each new visual beat exists because the owner's mechanism (transcript/consolidation.md, iteration 2) requires the mechanism to be SEEN — summaries chaining (repetition shown, twice), the extraction (three aspect streams pulled from the chain at the spoken words), compartments (session/job boxes; a second session joining). The carried compartments' choreography is untouched because the lines they serve survive verbatim; changing them would be revision without a reason — the register records the carry as a decision, not a default. EXPANSION #2 (2026-10-26, ~14:30 ET) replaced the expansion-#1 compartment design before it was built: the mega card / session-frame design is superseded pre-build by the sphere design (the owner's visual asset, provenance checked in consolidation §8.1 — the WS01 emblem, his 2026-10-22 description), and the compartments return as the zoom-out's job frames. Recorded here so the superseded design is a decision on record, not a disappearance.
scene_decomposition.record: scene/scene.json (phase 9 — per-compartment design record with carried / revised / new accounting)
scene_decomposition.source: archer reasoning (this branch, phase 8, 2026-10-26), derived from the iteration-2 story structure; embodied in scene/scene.json (phase 9)
scene_decomposition.value: ONE self-contained HTML file (the MP4 renders from this file alone). Compartments C1–C5 as prescribed in phase 2, carried in iteration 2 (the flat picture, the turn, the steering, the context stream, the accumulation pile — choreography untouched, since the lines they serve are untouched). C6 THE GATHERING, EXPANDED (iteration 2) — the mechanism is SHOWN, in four visual beats matching M6 (i–iv): the CHAIN SUMMARY CARD forms over the pile during the session's own time, a fold chip (the last stretch) flies in and the card's version ticks up — twice, so chaining is seen as repetition, not declared once; the EXTRACTION: three aspect cards are drawn out of the summary card in a stream at the spoken list — KEY DECISIONS / FEATURE REQUESTS / KEY CRITICISMS; the NAMING: summary + aspects bind into the MEGA PROMPT card, whose rows are now the three aspects and whose sub-line states the definition ('the prompt, summarized into its key aspects'); the NAMING is the DIRECTION SPHERE's formation (expansion #2): the aspect streams' arrows combine into the embedded vector of a wire sphere — the lane's direction emblem (WS01: wireframe ball + arrow) — under the cinematic label MEGA PROMPT; the USE: the sphere presides while its TEXT STREAM runs underneath the work area and a work arrow is checked against the sphere's vector — tilting into drift, pulled back onto the direction; the ZOOM-OUT: an injected ghost of the sphere flies to a new session at 'Inject', then the camera pulls back to a vista of job frames (JOB 1 / JOB 2 / JOB 3), each holding its own wire sphere with its own vector angle, under the caption 'ONE USER — EVERY JOB, ITS OWN DIRECTION'. C7 THE BRIDGE CARD (the Direction plug, phase-8 end_referral). Plus the standing compartments: the stage void, the lane furniture, the word-animation layer (now eleven line layers), the audio compartment, and the in-page decision-record layer. Semantic continuity extended, not broken: the pile's cards are what the summary summarizes (they ghost as their content enters it); the summary card is what the extraction draws from and what the mega prompt binds.

story_structure.rationale: Moves 1–5 stand as prescribed in phase 2 — the owner's iteration-1 verdict (60–70, 'getting better', direction holds) confirmed the spine, and his expansion targeted the transcript's gathering beats only. Iteration 1's M6 compressed the gathering into a single end-of-session act ('chain them into one summary'), which misstates the owner's mechanism in two ways his 2026-10-26 direction corrects: the chain summary is CONTINUAL (it forms during the session, each version combining the last stretch with the previous summary), and it is INSTRUCTED (the summary instruction is what derives the key aspects — decisions, feature requests, criticisms — and that extraction is what makes the mega prompt the DEFINED version of the prompt, not a heap of raw directions). The practice beat (iv) is his addition verbatim in substance: chain summaries are something a good agentic system builds, compartmentalized by session or job and building over multiple sessions — the piece now hands the viewer the practice, not only the definition. The payoff line survives iteration 1 verbatim as the closing verdict: the definition restated is still the piece's answer, and the bookend with M1 is untouched. EXPANSION #2 (2026-10-26, ~14:30 ET) restructured the tail again before any of it locked: the practice beat was REPLACED by the use beat and the zoom-out (restructuring over stacking, per his length discipline) — what the mega prompt does (runs underneath the work as a text stream; the agent continuously checked against its direction) and the vista it belongs to (many jobs, each with its own) are his; the full account is transcript/consolidation.md §8.
story_structure.record: phase-1 objective (this file); embodied in transcript/transcript.md (phase 3) and scene/scene.json (phase 4)
story_structure.source: archer reasoning (this branch, phase 2, 2026-10-26) for moves 1–5 + the owner's expansion (2026-10-26, ~14:22 ET) for M6, recorded in transcript/consolidation.md (iteration 2)
story_structure.value: Six moves, prescribed from the objective (moves 1–5 unchanged in iteration 2; M6 expanded by the owner's direction of 2026-10-26 ~14:22 ET): M1 THE FLAT PICTURE — the misconception stated as the viewer holds it (the prompt is the first sentence you type into the chat). M2 THE TURN — denial and definition in one breath: it is not; a prompt is a direction — it points the context somewhere. M3 THE STEERING, PERFORMED — one direction starts the work ('build me a page'), then the user steers again in fragments (warmer. Shorter. For my mother, not for engineers): directions as acts the viewer already performs. M4 THE CONTEXT UNDERNEATH — the mechanism: meanwhile the agent keeps producing the context — continuing it, compacting it — and every prompt you add bends it a new way. M5 ACCUMULATION — ABSORBED in iteration 2 (the standalone claim line retired on the measured length decision, consolidation §8.4): the accumulation is performed by M6's chain and restated by the payoff, with the pile and its counter playing across M6's opening. M6 THE GATHERING, TAUGHT AS A MECHANISM (iteration 2) — (i) THE CHAIN, DURING: as the session runs, a chain summary keeps forming — each version folds the last stretch into the one before; (ii) THE EXTRACTION: set the summary's instruction and it draws out the key aspects — the decisions, the feature requests, the criticisms; (iii) THE MEGA PROMPT, DEFINED: what you hold is the mega prompt — the prompt itself, summarized into all its key aspects; (iv) THE MEGA PROMPT IN USE (expansion #2): underneath the work, its text runs as a stream — and the agent is checked against it: on its direction, or drifting; (v) INJECTION + THE ZOOM-OUT (expansion #2): inject it into any session; keep one for every job — and the frame pulls back to a user with different jobs, each carrying its own mega prompt, each one a direction of its own; then the payoff restates the definition as the verdict, bookending M1 ('first sentence' returns as 'not one sentence'). The question the video answers (viewer-voiced): 'I typed my prompt at the start — was that the whole prompt?'

style_direction.rationale: The mix is derived from the jobs the objective assigns style: (a) the concept is an OBJECT story — directions are things that arrive, stack and bind — so the spine must be objects that persist and change role (motion graphics under the A59 grammar; timed word appearance alone cannot stack or bind); (b) the gathering and the payoff are VERDICTS, and the menu's instrument for verdict weight is cinematic type — rationed to those two moments so it stays weight and doesn't become wallpaper; (c) whiteboard was weighed and rejected: its classroom-sketch register argues against verdict weight, and a drawn line cannot carry the cutout object-identity the continuity law requires; collage rejected: texture noise competes with the word layer; 2D graphics as the named SPINE rejected: the work the objects do (persistence, role change, stacking, binding) is motion-graphics work — flat rendering is its hand, not its grammar. Both adopted styles are in the owner's starting set (#77).
style_direction.record: files/a59-motion-brief.md — LANE VERDICT (#78) + transferable grammar + STYLE MENU RULING (#77); embodied in scene/scene.json (phase 4)
style_direction.source: owner verdict #78 via files/a59-motion-brief.md (LANE VERDICT) — the lane input; archer reasoning (this branch, phase 2, 2026-10-26) for this piece's mix, from the phase-1 objective + files/a59-motion-brief.md (grammar + #77 starting set)
style_direction.value: LANE INPUT (owner-decided): the A59 grammar is the adopted direction for the Word Definitions lane — the owner's verdict #78 (2026-10-26), won on THIS piece's own exp-01 specimens (Variant B, 'more artistic'): independent textured cutouts on a dark void, one focal group, principal-word entry grammar (rise 24 units, scale 0.82→1 over 0.28 s, cubic ease-out), entries on the media clock at spoken words, SEMANTIC CONTINUITY as the core law. THIS PIECE'S MIX, decided against the objective: a MOTION GRAPHICS spine (the A59 object grammar above) + CINEMATIC TYPOGRAPHY at exactly two moments — the gathering (MEGA PROMPT at monumental scale) and the payoff line — because type's job here is verdict weight, not illustration. The cutouts render as flat 2D graphics (the menu's 2D graphics as the rendering hand, not a second style claim). Semantic continuity, prescribed: ONE prompt card is the scene's spine object — it enters as 'the prompt' (M1), is re-tagged the first direction (M2), is joined by sibling cards as the steering lands (M3), rides over the context stream it bends (M4), stacks with them (M5), and is bound with them into the mega prompt (M6); the context stream is the second persistent object — produced, extended, compacted, bent, never re-drawn.

scaffold_note: Decision scaffold for the FROM-SCRATCH rebuild of wd-02, opened 2026-10-26 (JOB REBUILD-WD02) under the owner's from-scratch order of the same day. This branch starts empty; nothing from the first build (branch video/wd-02 and the workspace records behind it) is copied as settled. The first build is EVIDENCE — consulted last, only for facts, raw material and what to avoid. Under the causal rule, every decision here cites the objective, the canon (files/canon.md) or the owner's recorded teachings as its source. Phase 1 decides the idea-level fields: objective, message, audience. The rest stands honestly OPEN with named routes. THE CONCEPT THIS PIECE TEACHES IS THE OWNER'S OWN, supplied 2026-10-26 ~11:50 ET after he rejected the first build's transcript as content ('not how I would describe what prompt is'): a prompt is a DIRECTION — as context is produced by the agent, continued and compacted, prompting is giving NEW DIRECTIONS; a prompt does not happen only at the beginning, it ACCUMULATES across the job; a session's prompts, chained into one summary, form a MEGA PROMPT — 'the prompt is not just one sentence, but all the directions that the user tries to re-steer the context in a different direction.' PHASE 2 (2026-10-26): architecture prescribed from the phase-1 objective — role, story structure (six moves), hook form, style direction (the lane's A59 adoption recorded as an owner-decided input, #78; this piece's mix decided against the objective), delivery pattern, end referral and scene form are all decided as prescription, not read off the first build. PHASE 3 (2026-10-26): transcript consolidated in the open — Candidate A drafted fresh from the phase-2 architecture FIRST (7 lines / 106 words), then weighed against Candidate B (this morning's redevelopment draft, built from the owner's definition, never verdicted by him) and the rejected i3 text (evidence only, read last). The settled text (8 lines / 128 spoken words) is recorded in transcript/transcript.md with the full per-line account in transcript/consolidation.md; the delivery pattern decided in phase 2 is sized as a pause map in transcript/delivery.md. Phase 3 also records the owner's TEXT RULE of 2026-10-26 ~13:24 ET: the word 'lives' is banned in any text destined for synthesis (the voices pronounce it as the plural of 'life', not the verb) — the settled text was checked against the ban: zero occurrences (see transcript/consolidation.md §7 and the phase-7 randomness register). ITERATION 2 (2026-10-26, phase 8): the owner's verdict on iteration 1 — 60–70, 'getting better', transcript still needs improvement — plus his expansion of the chain-summary mechanism (continual chaining; the instructed extraction of decisions / feature requests / criticisms; the mega prompt as a compartmentalized, cross-session practice; the Direction-video end relay). Objective, message, audience, role, hook and style stand UNCHANGED (the verdict confirmed them); story_structure (M6), delivery_structure, scene_decomposition (C6/C7) and end_referral are REVISED in this phase, each revision carrying its reason. The full feedback-impact analysis opens transcript/consolidation.md (iteration 2). EXPANSION #2 (same day, ~14:30 ET, phase 8 amendment): the mega prompt in use (stream underneath + continuous verification + injection), the zoom-out vista, the wire-sphere direction symbol as the mega prompt's visual identity, and his length discipline (restructure, don't stack) — story_structure and scene_decomposition revised accordingly; account in transcript/consolidation.md §8. LENGTH DECISION (phase 8, §8.4): with all takes measured (83.41 s with the claim line standing), L6 was weighed a second time and RETIRED under the owner's length discipline — the claim is performed by the chain and restated by the payoff; locked duration 75.024 s. M5 is absorbed into M6 in the story_structure field.
title: What Is a Prompt?
